originality.rationale: Originality is assessed for the joint stochastic domination and sharp (log n)/2 expected-cover advantage, not for the standard coupon marginal, known two-collector tie probability, or generic Gumbel limits. Full rendered primary text of the most plausible 2017 iid two-group source, the 2003 two-collector competition paper, and the 2020 multiple-walk cover source was compared at theorem/hypothesis level. No inspected result logically covers this periodic-vs-iid pair of claims; historical general de-Poissonization priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: Older de-Poissonization asymptotics for the maximum of multiple discrete coupon collectors might implicitly yield the same logarithmic coefficient without mentioning complete bipartite walks.

Absolute historical priority and independent mathematical review remain open.

value.rationale: The result quantifies the intrinsic effect of forced alternating side balance while holding all vertex marginal probabilities uniform: it proves uniform stochastic improvement at every horizon and resolves the first diverging mean correction to the classical coupon cover scale, with a sharp 1/2 coefficient. This natural second-order phenomenon is not a parameter rename or an arbitrary finite invariant.
